IBOV.title: Ibovespa
IBOV.body: The main index of B3, the Brazilian exchange. It tracks the most traded shares, weighted by the market value of the shares available for trading. Its portfolio is reviewed every four months.

IFIX.title: IFIX (real estate funds index)
IFIX.body: Tracks the most traded real estate funds listed on B3, counting both the change in unit prices and the income they distribute.

SMLL.title: Small Cap index (SMLL)
SMLL.body: Tracks B3's smaller companies: those outside the group of largest companies that together make up 85% of the exchange's market value.

IDIV.title: Dividend index (IDIV)
IDIV.body: Tracks the B3 shares with the highest dividend yields, by B3's criteria, counting dividends and interest on equity. Past distributions do not indicate future ones.

views.columnsHint: Tick the indicators you want to see. Your pick becomes “My view” and is kept in this browser.

YahooQuotes.combinedHint: Combined ranking: each company's positions in the selected columns are added up, lowest total first. Companies missing a value go last.
YahooQuotes.fundamentalsNote: Indicators from Yahoo Finance, trailing twelve months; tap ? on a column for how it is computed.

dy.title: DY (dividend yield)
dy.body: Dividends paid per share over the last twelve months, divided by the current price. Figures come from Yahoo Finance. Past payments, including one-off ones, do not indicate future payments.

pe.title: P/L (price to earnings)
pe.body: Share price divided by earnings per share over the last twelve months: how many years of current earnings the price represents. Figures come from Yahoo Finance. Empty when earnings are negative, and one-off gains or losses distort it.

pb.title: P/VP (price to book)
pb.body: Share price divided by book value (shareholders’ equity) per share. Figures come from Yahoo Finance. Book value follows accounting rules and may differ from what the assets are worth.

roe.title: ROE (return on equity)
roe.body: Net income of the last twelve months as a percentage of shareholders’ equity. Here it is computed as P/VP divided by P/L, from Yahoo Finance figures. Debt raises ROE without the business being more profitable.

roce.title: ROCE (return on capital employed)
roce.body: Operating profit (EBIT) of the last twelve months as a percentage of capital employed (total assets minus current liabilities), so it considers debt and equity together. Figures come from Yahoo Finance. Not shown for banks and insurers, whose balance sheets do not have this split.

evEbitda.title: EV/EBITDA (enterprise value to EBITDA)
evEbitda.body: Market value plus net debt, divided by EBITDA (earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation) of the last twelve months. It compares companies with different debt levels. Figures come from Yahoo Finance. Not shown for banks, which have no EBITDA.

netMargin.title: Net margin
netMargin.body: Net income of the last twelve months as a percentage of revenue: what is left of every 100 of revenue. Figures come from Yahoo Finance. One-off gains or losses distort it, and bank revenue is not comparable with other companies.

netDebtEbitda.title: Net debt / EBITDA
netDebtEbitda.body: Debt minus cash, divided by EBITDA of the last twelve months: how many years of operating cash generation would repay the debt. Negative means more cash than debt. Figures come from Yahoo Finance, which does not count leases as debt, so the number can be lower than the one the company reports. Not shown for banks.

profitGrowth.title: Profit growth (3 years)
profitGrowth.body: Average yearly growth of net income between the oldest and the latest fiscal year available on Yahoo Finance (four fiscal years, so three years). Empty when either end is a loss. For companies Yahoo reports in dollars, the growth is in dollars. Past results do not indicate future results.

payout.title: Payout (share of profit distributed)
payout.body: Dividends of the last twelve months as a percentage of earnings of the same period. Here it is computed as DY times P/L, from Yahoo Finance figures. Above 100% the company paid out more than it earned in the period.

liquidity.title: Daily liquidity
liquidity.body: Average value traded per day over the last 21 sessions (closing price times shares traded), in the quote currency. Figures come from Yahoo Finance. K = thousand, M = million, B = billion.

YahooQuotes.commoditiesNote: Nearest-expiry futures contracts via Yahoo Finance, delayed. Each price is in the unit shown next to the name: bbl = barrel, oz = troy ounce (31.1 g), lb = pound (0.454 kg), bu = bushel (about 27 kg of soybeans or wheat, 25 kg of corn), t = tonne, MMBtu = million British thermal units, US¢ = US cents. gal = US gallon (3.785 litres), st = short ton (907 kg), cwt = hundredweight (45.4 kg), mbf = thousand board feet (about 2.36 m³ of lumber).
